clue.text: One taking steps to record driver originally going through sign

indicators.note: the record and the driver's first letter pass right through the middle of the star sign

parts.note: Cancer is a sign of the zodiac
to log is to record

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of driver

parts.note: first letter of driver

explanation.surface: A traffic warden noting a motorist cutting across a road sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sign' is a zodiac sign, not a road sign as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog dancer performs rhythmic steps in wooden shoes, so is literally someone taking steps.

clue.text: A good rave largely annoyed an Italian law man

indicators.note: annoyed means stirred up or disturbed, so the letters before it are jumbled
largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a rave is a dance party; here just its letters

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by a noisy all-night dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an Italian law man' is a scientist, not a lawyer: the law is a law of physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the Italian scientist behind Avogadro's law about gas volumes and molecules.

clue.text: Was effective around left — that bloke's happy

indicators.note: the past-tense verb goes around the abbreviation for left

parts.note: bit is the past of bite, to take effect, as brakes do
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A man cheerful because something he did worked out well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was effective' is the past of bite in its sense of taking effect, as when a new rule bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerful and carefree, a literary synonym for happy.

clue.text: Complain about one 'inadvertently misleading' Parliament?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the verb is read from the end back

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a politician whose claim to have misled the House by accident is doubted.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs who mislead the House often claim it was inadvertent; the quote marks and question mark suggest the setter thinks otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who misleads Parliament, however innocently they claim it was, is called by the setter what they are: a teller of untruths.

clue.text: Crop expert disheartened fighting simpleton over time

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble or fighting

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme is the proverbial simpleton

explanation.surface: A farming adviser dismayed by a fool brawling past closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGRO (British slang for fighting) loses its middle G to give AGRO; Simple Simon from the nursery rhyme stands for a simpleton and is reversed to NOMIS; T ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: An agronomist is a scientist who studies soil management and crop production.

clue.text: Movies (American) shot at one time in this …

definitions.text: Movies (American) shot at one time in this

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken up, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of American are the fodder

explanation.surface: Hollywood films were once made using this format, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed word is both fodder and part of the picture; the ellipsis carries the sentence into 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerama was a widescreen process using three cameras, used for some 1950s and 1960s films.

clue.text: … horror one for PM's 'closest adviser'?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1976 horror film ..., from Stephen King's novel
second meaning: ... Johnson, wife of Prime Minister Boris Johnson, said to be his closest confidante

explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks hint at reports that Carrie Symonds held great sway in Downing Street.
explanation.definitionFit: The same first name belongs both to a famous horror film title and to the Prime Minister's then partner.

clue.text: See 9
Making flat denial at first, then have to reveal a U-turn in government policy?

parts.note: levelling is making a surface flat

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of denial

parts.note: first letter of denial
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A government flatly denies, then is forced to admit, that it has abandoned a flagship policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson's government's slogan was 'levelling up'; its opposite is the U-turn the question mark jokes about.
explanation.definitionFit: Levelling down, reducing everyone to the same lower level, is the reverse of the 'levelling up' agenda.

clue.text: Said one was equipped for work in the Garden State

indicators.note: said means the phrase is spoken, giving the sound of the entered word

parts.words: one was equipped for work in the Garden
parts.note: "I'd a hoe": I had a hoe, the tool for garden work

explanation.surface: Someone recalling being kitted out for a job in New Jersey, known as the Garden State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Garden State' looks like the definition (it is New Jersey's nickname) but Garden belongs to the wordplay and State alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the north-west.

clue.text: Nameless criminal and comic

indicators.note: without a name means the abbreviation N for name is removed

parts.note: a gangster is a member of a criminal gang

explanation.surface: An anonymous crook who is also a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name, so 'Nameless' drops it from GANGSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is a writer or teller of jokes, so a comedian.

clue.text: Heavily beaten by mistress (face obscured) with belt

indicators.note: with its face hidden the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a mistress is a lover
to belt is to run at speed

explanation.surface: A dominatrix, her face masked, thrashing someone with a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' looks like a strap but is the verb, to belt along.
explanation.definitionFit: An army overrun has been overwhelmed and defeated by the enemy, so routed.

clue.text: Confuse with nonsense — initially, they wouldn't leave

indicators.note: the letters named go away from the word for nonsense

parts.note: twaddle is nonsense

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: first letter of they
first letter of wouldn't

explanation.surface: Bamboozling visitors with drivel, though they still refuse to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'they wouldn't leave' becomes an instruction: the initial letters T and W leave TWADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle or befuddle someone's mind.

clue.text: One may come up with 'The Future's Green', also 'Green Revolution'

definitions.text: One may come up with 'The Future's Green'

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of green

explanation.surface: A political advertiser coining environmental slogans for a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Revolution' reads as a second slogan, but it is the anagram of ALSO plus GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloganeer is someone who devises catchy promotional phrases, such as an advertising copywriter.

clue.text: Mark and Charlie worse off without — they're not exactly smart in their field

definitions.text: they're not exactly smart in their field

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two men, Mark and Charlie, worse off for going without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark and Charlie' look like names; Mark gives SCAR and Charlie gives C, mixed with WORSE to make ECROWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarecrows stand in farm fields in ragged old clothes, hardly smartly dressed and not clever either.

clue.text: On motorway, transport's beginning to conk out — hitching again!

parts.note: re means on, concerning
M is the abbreviation for a British motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: the first letter of the word stops working and drops away

parts.note: a carriage is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A car breaking down on the motorway, leaving its driver to hitch a lift again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitching' looks like hitchhiking; it means getting hitched, married.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is informal for marrying, so doing so again is a second marriage.

clue.text: Conservative pals may coin it freely — that's about right with this

definitions.text: Conservative pals may coin it freely — that's about right with this

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so the letters are rearranged at will

explanation.surface: A wry comment that Tory friends cashing in on government contracts is what you'd expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PALS MAY COIN IT with C and R gives the answer, while the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crony capitalism is an economy where business success depends on close ties with politicians, letting friends of the government profit.

clue.text: Cry due to looking old

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
owed means due, as a debt

explanation.surface: Someone weeping because they are showing their age.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper and fabric go yellowed as they age, so the word describes something showing its years.

clue.text: Inherit a settlement, generally felt to be imminent

indicators.note: a settlement re-settles the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Coming into money from a legacy that everyone senses is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' looks like a legal payout belonging with 'Inherit'; it signals the anagram of INHERIT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the air is sensed by many as about to happen, an idiom for a widely felt mood.

clue.text: One right suppressed among others — tough!

indicators.note: held down inside the word for others, so the pieces go within it

parts.note: the rest means the others
I is the Roman numeral one
a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A lone voice of the right silenced by the others, who show no mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like R but is LIEN, a legal right over property.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient people are hardy and recover from setbacks, so tough in character.

clue.text: Finally register wrong family

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
kin are family

explanation.surface: Getting round to signing up with an errant relative.
explanation.definitionFit: When a fact sinks in, it is at last understood, so it eventually registers in the mind.

clue.text: Are talk shows being withdrawn next?

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the letters read in reverse
shows means the letters are on display within the words

explanation.surface: Asking whether chat shows are being cancelled next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk shows' looks like TV programmes; 'shows' displays the letters in ARE TAL(K) and 'being withdrawn' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means after this, coming next in time.

clue.text: Boy gets lots of information in a letter

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy
MB is a megabyte, a large amount of computer data

explanation.surface: A boy receiving a great deal of news in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a letter' looks like the place the information arrives; 'in' is the insertion and 'letter' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Talked of private grudge

indicators.note: talked of means as spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: A soldier speaking about a personal resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent RANKER and RANCOUR sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-held resentment, the same as a grudge.

clue.text: Wake up hearing arguments

indicators.note: hearing means as heard, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: to rouse is to wake someone up

explanation.surface: Being woken by the sound of people quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Here ROWS rhymes with cows, not with toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows are noisy quarrels, so the word means disputes.

clue.text: After year out, south coast team's internationals destroyed City

indicators.note: out means the year abbreviation leaves the word

parts.note: Pompey is the nickname of Portsmouth, an English south coast football club
I is the abbreviation for international, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Portsmouth's international players beating Manchester City after a year away.
explanation.walkthrough: Pompey is the nickname of Portsmouth, a south coast English town and football club; 'City' looks like a rival team.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman city buried and destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Green area is quiet place of refuge

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
Noah's ark was a refuge from the flood

explanation.surface: Describing a park as a tranquil sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A park is a public open space of grass and trees in a town.

clue.text: Abandon a lot of mates outside America

indicators.note: the shortened word for mates sits outside the abbreviation for America
a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: wives are mates, marriage partners

explanation.surface: Deserting most of one's friends while abroad from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mates' looks like friends but means spouses: WIVES, cut to WIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive a right or claim is to give it up voluntarily, to relinquish it.

clue.text: On the job with lady occasionally entertained — which a certain politician aspired to be?

definitions.text: which a certain politician aspired to be?

indicators.note: entertained means taken in as a guest, so the letters go inside

parts.note: working means on the job

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of lady

parts.note: alternate letters of lady

explanation.surface: An innuendo about an affair at work, linked to a politician's ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson said as a child that he wanted to be 'world king'; the surface hints at his affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson's sister recalled that his childhood ambition was to become ruler of the whole world.
